doc.title: Maria Schneider interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001

title: Success, unexpected career and nearly studying astrophysics
summary: She never expected her career, imagined being a waitress or copyist, and nearly switched majors to astrophysics.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. It’s not your job. Wow. I’ll shorten this one up, but it says, “love of music doesn’t always manifest itself in the wish to make money as a musician. Having a monstrous career is not a marking stick for being successful.” That’s a heavy statement.

Yeah, there’s a lot of great composers that weren’t really discovered in their lifetime that much, the Charles Ives and people who went a great portion of their life being really unrecognized yet were strong in developing what they did. It didn’t really change anything for them. I mean easy to say, because I’ve been lucky that way. But I have to say I didn’t expect to have the career that I have. I actually didn’t even set out to do it. I kind of expected, I honestly, people laugh and they think that I’m joking, but I honestly expected that maybe I’d have to be a waitress. I’ve been a waitress before. I was a truck stop waitress, that I’d be a music copyist maybe for a really long time, maybe forever. That maybe I’d have to do other things. And then I’d write and do my thing on the side on my own. So the fact that, actually I got a little bit worried when I did start making a living because I thought oh my God I’m going to get commissioned and then I’m going

to feel like I have to do this. And I always wanted to do what I’m doing because I want to. I don’t, you know if I decided I didn’t want to write music — I doubt it would happen but it could — that if I wanted to quit and just do something else, say I just suddenly got interested in something else creatively, I would just do that. In college I almost switched majors to astrophysics.
I wasn’t smart enough, but I really, I took an astronomy course, physics and astronomy, and I was so interested in that, and I really came close to changing my major.
